description: Short coding prompts the way a coding harness sends them: a system prompt is always present; tool_prompts are sent with the tools offered.
system: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside a coding harness. Answer concisely and show code in fenced blocks. When tools are available, use them to read, write and edit files and to run commands instead of guessing.
prompts: Write a Python function that reverses a string.

Fix the off-by-one in this loop:
```python
for i in range(1, len(items)):
    print(items[i])
```
It should print every item.
Give me a one-line shell command that counts the lines in every .py file under the current directory.
How do I undo the last git commit but keep the changes staged? One line.

Give me a unified diff that renames the variable tmp to total in:
```python
def add(xs):
    tmp = 0
    for x in xs:
        tmp += x
    return tmp
```
Write a Rust function that returns the sum of a slice of i32.

Explain in two sentences what this does:
```bash
find . -name '*.log' -mtime +7 -delete
```

Convert this to a list comprehension:
```python
out = []
for x in xs:
    if x % 2 == 0:
        out.append(x * x)
```
Write a SQL query that returns the 5 most recent rows from the table orders by created_at.
What is the time complexity of binary search, and why? Two sentences.
tool_prompts: Create hello.py that prints hello world.
Run the test suite with pytest and tell me whether it passes.
Read README.md and tell me what the project does.
In utils.py rename the function foo to bar.

function.name: write
function.description: Write a file to disk, replacing it.

function.name: edit
function.description: Replace one exact occurrence of old_text with new_text in a file.

function.name: bash
function.description: Run a shell command and return its output.
